summary: Every review-4 course finding was fixed in the text as asked: the tasks that were descriptions now have data inside the prompt and run in a free tool, minutes add up against the stated task times, the over-full cards in M5, M6 and M7 are split with worked cases (the figures re-check), and M1's outcome now covers the whole module. The nine changed questions solve without the key and are taught by their cards without copying the cards' own example; the three blind misses are ruled on and the key stands for all three, including the rewritten m10-q3. check.mjs is clean, no finding is must-fix, and every module scores at least 4 on every dimension (seven modules rose). What is left is small: M4 t2's six-row run is empty, M5 t1's hint is wrong about Meena, M7 t1 needs two commands no card teaches, two M7 question titles don't match their cases, and the blueprint still describes the old tasks and an older clue-test run.
strengths: The task rebuilds are real and checkable. Each has data in the prompt, a free route, minutes, and a hint that gives the answer to check; the figures all re-add (COD 60%, Card 33%, UPI 25%; 8 rows become 7; Card 2300, Wallet 800, UPI 570; Travel 5,200, Food 1,450, Grocery 450; 9,900 becomes 17,600; ₹32.6 lakh against ₹32 lakh).
M6's new worked test is statistically right: 160 of 4,000 against 200 of 4,000 gives p about 0.03, and 4.0% against 4.3% about 0.5. M7's six leads and merchants join behave as the hints say.

The nine changed questions: each has one clear best answer, the wrong options are named mistakes (ascending sort, wrong partition, month-first dates, 'and' without brackets, a log scale, an average time against a rate target), and none repeats its card's own numbers.
Rules 10 and 11 hold: m01-q1, f05 and m10-q1 each state the fact that makes the sensible extra step pointless.
M5 and M6 now show results beside their code and figures, and M10 card 2's profit example follows rule 14 (₹10 lakh at 40% is ₹4 lakh, less ₹1.5 lakh is ₹2.5 lakh).

findings.problem: M4 t2 now asks the learner to run the HAVING COUNT(*) >= 50 query on a deliveries table of six rows. With six rows every city has fewer than 50 delivered orders, so the result is empty and "check whether the result matches what you said" tests nothing.
findings.fix: End t2 with: "Then create a deliveries table of your own with six rows (city, status, delivery_minutes), change 50 to 2 in the query, run it, and check that the result matches what you said."

findings.problem: M5 t1's hint says "Meena signed up in 2025, so she is left out". Meena has orders 103 and 104, so she is left out because she has ordered, not because of her sign-up year. No row in the data tests the 2026 sign-up filter, which the task asks for, and the blueprint's competent result filters on signed_up.
findings.fix: Add a sixth customer to the insert list, (6,'Farah','Delhi','2025-12-05'), with no orders. Change the hint's check to: "the result is Ravi and Imran. Farah never ordered but signed up in 2025, so the 2026 filter leaves her out; Asha, Meena and Sana have orders." t2 and M9 t1 are unaffected (Farah has no orders).

findings.problem: M7 t1 asks for May 2026 transactions by category, highest first, but no card shows how to sort descending (sort_values) or pick a month out of a date column (.dt.month, or comparing dates). A beginner on a phone is stuck for the 40 minutes. The same gap holds for t3, which needs a small table built with pd.DataFrame, shown nowhere.
findings.fix: Add to t1's hint: "After pd.to_datetime(..., dayfirst=True), df[\"txn_time\"].dt.month == 5 picks May; .sort_values(ascending=False) puts the largest first." Add to t3's prompt: "Build the merchants table the way task 1 built the transactions: paste it as text and read it with pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(...))."

findings.problem: Two titles don't match their questions. m07-q3 is titled "Guest checkouts" but its case is coupon codes removed from a coupons table; m07-q4 is titled "Large successful payments" but its case is Pune cab bookings with a fare above ₹800. Learners see the title first.
findings.fix: Retitle m07-q3 "Removed coupon codes" and m07-q4 "Pune fares above ₹800" (and update the blueprint's rows if they quote the titles).

findings.problem: The blueprint is behind the file in two places. (1) Clue-test record: line 296 says the clue tests ran "on the round-2 version"; line 301 and the known-defects list (line 305) say the nine round-4 questions "haven't been clue-tested in their new form"; the Inputs line says blind 54 of 55 "run on the file before this round's question edits". probes.json now holds a run on this exact version: cards 40 of 40, options 39 of 55, blind 52 of 55 (m01-q1, m08-q4, m10-q3 chosen differently). (2) The Practical evidence table (lines 142 to 160) still describes the old written tasks: "M2 t1 Plan a PivotTable", "M3 t1 Cleaning plan", "M7 t1 Plan the notebook", "M8 t1 Sketch the dashboard", "M9 t1 Prompt and checks", and M4, M5 and M6 are the same. The tasks are now hands-on with data in the prompt, so the competent-result column no longer matches the work a mentor will see.
findings.fix: Update the Inputs line, the clue-test section and the known defects to the latest run, and say the nine round-4 questions were clue-tested (all nine answered as keyed in the blind run except m10-q3, ruled on in review 5: the key stands). Rewrite the Practical evidence rows for M2 to M9 around the tasks as they now read, taking the expected results from the hints (COD 60%, Card 33%, UPI 25%; 8 rows become 7; Card 2300 / Wallet 800 / UPI 570; Ravi and Imran; Travel 5,200, Food 1,450, Grocery 450; total 9,900 becomes 17,600; ₹32.6 lakh against ₹32 lakh; 2 of 3 customers).

findings.problem: m10-q3 is keyed correctly (see probe_leads) but the blind test picked the first option because "re-check in September" sounds careful and its date is vague: for next June's stock a September re-check comes after the decision.
findings.fix: Change that option to "Say the weeks may not be typical of the year, and that the plan should wait for a second year of data" so it is clearly the over-caveat. Keep it within a few characters of the key's length.

findings.problem: m08-q4 was picked differently in the blind run ("show both figures side by side"). The owner's definition rules it out, but the scenario doesn't say she wants a single figure.
findings.fix: Add to the scenario: "She wants one repeat-customer rate on the page."

findings.problem: Every task hint now ends with a "Check:" line giving the right answer. That helps a learner who has finished, but it sits in the hint, so a stuck learner meets the answer before trying.
findings.fix: Show the check after the learner submits, as review 4 suggested; until the engine can do that, begin it with "Only after you have tried: " so it reads as a check, not a clue.

findings.problem: Carried from review 4: card 3 doesn't mention that the DPDP Rules, 2025 bring most duties in by stages up to 2027.
findings.fix: After checking the Gazette dates, add "The DPDP Rules, 2025 bring most duties in by stages up to 2027." to card 3.

findings.problem: Carried from review 4: m10-q1's key gives the cost of the problem (₹4 lakh a month) but not the size of the action, though card 1 asks for "its size in ₹".
findings.fix: Optionally end the key with "...in every Tier-3 city: the six-city trial cut COD returns from 31% to 19%." and check it is not strictly the longest option.

findings.problem: M8 card 3 uses "DAX" and "paid capacity" without explaining them, and Power BI Desktop is Windows-only; a phone-only learner can do both tasks in Sheets but not the card's example.
findings.fix: Write "DAX (Power BI's formula language)" at first use, and add "Windows-only: on a phone or Mac, do the same work in Looker Studio or Google Sheets."

findings.problem: Answer integrity, carried from rounds 1 to 4: every student sees the options in the same order, and the project has no pass rule or rubric weights in the engine.
findings.fix: Paul to decide, as in the blueprint's "For the team" items 1 and 3.

probe_leads.ruling: Dismissed, key upheld, re-ruled on the text. The founder names the decision (where extra riders go), the measure (share of orders within 30 minutes, against 90%), the breakdown (each city) and the period (four weeks); M1 card 1 says a request that names these is ready. Asking spends one of the two days on answered questions.

Dismissed. The marketing head owns the dashboard and has defined a repeat customer as one who ordered before the quarter; the 74% measures something else, so the measure should be fixed and checked against the 41%. Side by side suits two teams with two agreed definitions. Idea raised to make 'one rate on the page' explicit.

Dismissed, key upheld. The decision is next June's reopening and the data is two reopening weeks, so they are the right evidence; M10 card 3 says so for Diwali. 'Not typical of the year' is true but doesn't bear on the decision, and the key states the limit that does (one season). The rewrite did not add a second right answer: the first option's only support is a vague 'September' re-check. Idea raised to tighten that option.
Dismissed: the survey option tests preference, but the goal is scores and the test measured them; the random assignment is stated.
Dismissed: the scenario says the scale is balanced (two positive, two negative choices).
Dismissed: the definition-only prompt names no table columns, so the assistant must invent them (M9 card 1).
Dismissed: the assistant never saw the schema, so asking again can only produce another guess; the key supplies the definitions.
Dismissed: the six-city random trial has already run, so another test is pointless.
Dismissed: Shillong is a tourist town, so its sales follow other visitors; arithmetic re-adds (38 x 60% = 23; 61 x 60% = 37; 45 x 60% = 27; 20 x 60% = 12).
Dismissed: 'most new customers' ignores the ₹12 lakh spent and the decision to move budget.
Dismissed: the margin-of-error option never tells the funder that 600 households are missing (M3 card 3), and the report is due next week.
Dismissed: the test ran its planned 21 days; extending it is peeking.
Dismissed: 84 against 75 sales out of 3,000 is within chance (z about 0.7), so holding back loses a clear gain.
Dismissed: the opening names no action or number (M10 card 1); the clinics were chosen at random.

lessons.rule: After changing a task to run on a small table, run the task as written: check that every filter, threshold or condition in the given query still has rows to act on at that size.
lessons.why: M4 t2's HAVING COUNT(*) >= 50 on a six-row table returns nothing.

lessons.rule: When a hint explains why a row is excluded, check the row against the data, not the reason you expect; give each filter a row that only that filter removes.
lessons.why: M5 t1's hint said Meena was left out for her 2025 sign-up, but she was left out because she has orders, so the sign-up filter was never tested.
